-## Kotlin
-| Concept | What it is | First seen |
-| Trailing lambdas / type-safe builders | A lambda passed last can sit outside `()`; Gradle's `plugins { }` blocks are function calls | [build.gradle.kts](notes/build.gradle.kts.md) |
-| Final by default | Classes and functions are `final` unless `open`; the `plugin.spring` compiler plugin opens Spring beans | [build.gradle.kts](notes/build.gradle.kts.md) |

-| Final is not immutable | `open`/`final` controls subclassing and overriding; `val`/`var` controls mutability. A final method under a Spring proxy fails silently | [build.gradle.kts](notes/build.gradle.kts.md) |
-| Platform types and `-Xjsr305=strict` | How Java nullability annotations become real `T` / `T?` types | [build.gradle.kts](notes/build.gradle.kts.md) |
-| Class with no body | `class InventoryApplication` needs no braces | [InventoryApplication.kt](notes/main/InventoryApplication.kt.md) |
-| Top-level functions | `fun main` lives outside any class; compiled into `InventoryApplicationKt` | [InventoryApplication.kt](notes/main/InventoryApplication.kt.md) |
-| Reified type parameters | `runApplication<T>()`, `withType<Test>`: the type in `<>` instead of `T::class.java` | [InventoryApplication.kt](notes/main/InventoryApplication.kt.md) |
-| Infix functions | `a version b` means `a.version(b)` | [build.gradle.kts](notes/build.gradle.kts.md) |
-| `Array<String>` | Kotlin's `String[]`: an ordinary generic class | [InventoryApplication.kt](notes/main/InventoryApplication.kt.md) |
-| Spread operator `*` | Pass an array's elements as a vararg | [InventoryApplication.kt](notes/main/InventoryApplication.kt.md) |
-| Named arguments | `proxyBeanMethods = false`, also in annotations | [TestcontainersConfiguration.kt](notes/test/support/TestcontainersConfiguration.kt.md) |
-| Expression bodies | `fun f(): T = expr` instead of `{ return expr }` | [TestcontainersConfiguration.kt](notes/test/support/TestcontainersConfiguration.kt.md) |
-| Class references `X::class` | Kotlin's version of Java's `X.class` | [InventoryApplicationTests.kt](notes/test/InventoryApplicationTests.kt.md) |
-| `internal` vs package-private | Kotlin has no package-private; `internal` = same Gradle module | [README](../../README.md#project-layout) |
-| Public by default | No modifier means `public` (Java: package-private); helpers must say `private` | [InventoryRepositoryTest.kt](notes/test/inventory/InventoryRepositoryTest.kt.md) |
-| `@Autowired constructor` | Annotating the primary constructor needs the `constructor` keyword | [InventoryRepositoryTest.kt](notes/test/inventory/InventoryRepositoryTest.kt.md) |
-| Backtick function names | `` fun `reads like a sentence`() `` for test names | [InventoryRepositoryTest.kt](notes/test/inventory/InventoryRepositoryTest.kt.md) |
-| `kotlin.test` assertions | `assertEquals`, `assertTrue`, `assertFailsWith<T> { }` | [InventoryRepositoryTest.kt](notes/test/inventory/InventoryRepositoryTest.kt.md) |
-| Extension functions | `fun MockMvc.get(...)`: a function added to a class from outside it | [InventoryControllerTest.kt](notes/test/inventory/InventoryControllerTest.kt.md) |
-| Raw strings `"""` | Multi-line strings without escaping; `trimIndent()` to strip indentation | [InventoryControllerTest.kt](notes/test/inventory/InventoryControllerTest.kt.md) |
-| Primary constructor properties | `class X(private val dep: Dep)`: declares and assigns a property in the constructor | [InventoryRepository.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryRepository.kt.md) |
-| Read-only `List` vs `MutableList` | `List` has no `add`/`remove`; callers get a snapshot | [InventoryRepository.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryRepository.kt.md) |

-| Lambdas, `_` and SAM conversion | `{ rs, _ -> ... }` stands in for Java's single-method `RowMapper`; `_` = unused parameter | [InventoryRepository.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryRepository.kt.md) |

-| A lambda's last expression is its return value | `.query { }` / `.map { }` call the lambda once per element and collect what it returns | [InventoryRepository.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryRepository.kt.md) |
-| KDoc vs `// Why:` | KDoc (`/** */`) says what, for callers, shown on hover; `// Why:` says why, for maintainers | [InventoryRepository.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryRepository.kt.md) |

-| JSpecify nullability from Java | Spring 7's `@Nullable` makes `query(Class)` yield `T?`; a row-mapper lambda keeps `T` non-null | [InventoryRepository.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryRepository.kt.md) |
-| `data class` | Generated `equals`/`hashCode`/`toString`/`copy`/`componentN` from constructor properties; Kotlin's Java `record` | [InventoryItem.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryItem.kt.md) |

-| `==` vs `===`, and `copy` | `==` calls `equals` (value equality for data classes); `===` is identity. `copy` returns a new object and leaves the original alone | [InventoryItem.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryItem.kt.md) |
-| No checked exceptions | Kotlin has no `throws` clause; unchecked `DataAccessException` travels up to a `500` | [InventoryService.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryService.kt.md) |

-| Nullable types `T?` | `InventoryItem?` = an item or `null`; the compiler makes you handle `null` before use. Kotlin's built-in `Optional` | [InventoryRepository.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryRepository.kt.md) |

-| `singleOrNull` / `single` / `firstOrNull` | Zero-or-one lookups on a list; `singleOrNull` returns `null` (no exception) for 0 *or* 2+ elements | [InventoryRepository.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryRepository.kt.md) |
-| Elvis operator `?:` | `a ?: b` = `a` unless it's `null`, then `b` | [InventoryService.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryService.kt.md) |
-| `throw` as an expression, `Nothing` | `x ?: throw E()` has the non-null type of `x`; `Nothing` fits any type | [InventoryService.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryService.kt.md) |

-| KDoc block tags (`@throws`) | Tags start their own line; `@throws` is how a signature announces an exception without checked exceptions | [InventoryService.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryService.kt.md) |
-| Extending a class | `class A(x: T) : B(...)` = `extends B` plus the `super(...)` call | [SkuNotFoundException.kt](notes/main/inventory/error/SkuNotFoundException.kt.md) |
-| Plain constructor parameters | No `val`/`var` = usable only during construction, not a property | [SkuNotFoundException.kt](notes/main/inventory/error/SkuNotFoundException.kt.md) |

-| Storage vs visibility | `val` decides whether a constructor parameter is kept; `private` decides who can read it. `private val` enforces the layers | [SkuNotFoundException.kt](notes/main/inventory/error/SkuNotFoundException.kt.md) |
-| No ternary; `if` is an expression | Java's `c ? a : b` is `if (c) a else b`; `?:` (Elvis) only tests for `null` | [InventoryService.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryService.kt.md) |
-| String templates | `"SKU not found: $skuId"`, and `${expr}` for anything longer than a name | [SkuNotFoundException.kt](notes/main/inventory/error/SkuNotFoundException.kt.md) |
-| Nullable values from Java | `Throwable.message` is `String?` because `getMessage()` may return null | [InventoryExceptionHandler.kt](notes/main/inventory/error/InventoryExceptionHandler.kt.md) |

-| Concept | What it is | First seen |

-| Connection details | Compose / Testcontainers supply the DB connection, overriding `spring.datasource.*` | [application.yml](notes/main/resources/application.yml.md) |
-| Test context caching | Identical test configurations share one context (and container) until the run ends | [TestcontainersConfiguration.kt](notes/test/support/TestcontainersConfiguration.kt.md) |
-| `@TestConfiguration` + `@Import` | Test-only beans that component scanning skips | [TestcontainersConfiguration.kt](notes/test/support/TestcontainersConfiguration.kt.md) |
-| `@ServiceConnection` | A Testcontainers container supplies DataSource connection details | [TestcontainersConfiguration.kt](notes/test/support/TestcontainersConfiguration.kt.md) |
-| `@SpringBootTest` | Starts the full application context in a test | [InventoryApplicationTests.kt](notes/test/InventoryApplicationTests.kt.md) |
-| Exception translation | SQL errors become `DataAccessException`s, e.g. `DataIntegrityViolationException` | [InventoryRepositoryTest.kt](notes/test/inventory/InventoryRepositoryTest.kt.md) |
-| `@JdbcTest` slice | JDBC-only context, no component scan, each test rolled back | [InventoryRepositoryTest.kt](notes/test/inventory/InventoryRepositoryTest.kt.md) |
-| `@AutoConfigureMockMvc` + Kotlin MockMvc DSL | In-process HTTP requests; `mockMvc.get(...).andExpect { }` | [InventoryControllerTest.kt](notes/test/inventory/InventoryControllerTest.kt.md) |
-| `JsonCompareMode.STRICT` | Exact JSON match: no extra fields, array order matters | [InventoryControllerTest.kt](notes/test/inventory/InventoryControllerTest.kt.md) |

-| Flyway migrations | `V<n>__<desc>.sql` (two underscores) in `db/migration`, run once at startup, checksummed; wrong names are skipped silently | [V1__create_inventory.sql](notes/main/resources/db/migration/V1__create_inventory.sql.md) |

-| Migrations are changes, not snapshots | A schema change is a new `V2__` with `ALTER TABLE`; the schema is the whole V1→Vn chain | [V1__create_inventory.sql](notes/main/resources/db/migration/V1__create_inventory.sql.md) |

-| Component scanning and stereotypes | `@Repository`/`@Service`/`@RestController` make scanned classes beans; `@Import` registers one by hand | [InventoryRepository.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryRepository.kt.md) |
-| Constructor injection | A single constructor is autowired without `@Autowired`; beans are created at startup | [InventoryRepository.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryRepository.kt.md) |
-| `JdbcClient` query chain | `sql(...)` prepares, `query { row mapper }` maps, `list()` runs and collects | [InventoryRepository.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryRepository.kt.md) |

-| `@RestController` vs `@Controller` | `@RestController` = `@Controller` + `@ResponseBody`: return values are written as the body, not rendered as views | [InventoryController.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryController.kt.md) |
-| `@RequestMapping` + `@GetMapping` | Class-level base path plus method-level mappings; the function name doesn't matter | [InventoryController.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryController.kt.md) |
-| Message converters (Jackson) | A `@ResponseBody` value is written as JSON; Kotlin property names become JSON keys | [InventoryController.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryController.kt.md) |
-| The service layer | Business rules and error mapping sit between HTTP (controller) and SQL (repository) | [InventoryService.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryService.kt.md) |

-| Singleton beans and threads | One bean instance, built at startup, serves every request thread at once, so beans must be stateless | [InventoryController.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryController.kt.md) |
-| Named parameters in SQL | `:skuId` + `.param("skuId", value)` binds the value separately, preventing SQL injection | [InventoryRepository.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryRepository.kt.md) |

-| `@PathVariable` and path templates | `@GetMapping("/{skuId}")` matches one path segment and binds it to the same-named parameter | [InventoryController.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryController.kt.md) |

-| Exception resolver chain | Spring catches every controller exception: `@ExceptionHandler` (controller, then advice) → `@ResponseStatus` → built-in mappings → `500` | [InventoryExceptionHandler.kt](notes/main/inventory/error/InventoryExceptionHandler.kt.md) |

-| When mistakes surface | Compile time (types), startup (missing beans), first request (strings: paths, SQL, missing advice); only request-level tests catch the last | [InventoryController.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryController.kt.md) |

-| `ResponseEntity` builder | `status(...).contentType(...).body(...)` sets status, headers and body; `notFound()` has no body | [InventoryExceptionHandler.kt](notes/main/inventory/error/InventoryExceptionHandler.kt.md) |

+# Kotlin & Spring Concepts Index
+A running index of every Kotlin and Spring concept used in this codebase. Each row links to
+the study notes that explain it in full (see [notes/README.md](notes/README.md)). `/sync-docs`
+and `/walkthrough` add rows as new concepts come up.
+## Kotlin
+| Concept | What it is | First seen |
+| Trailing lambdas / type-safe builders | A lambda passed last can sit outside `()`; Gradle's `plugins { }` blocks are function calls | [build.gradle.kts](notes/build.gradle.kts.md) |
+| Final by default | Classes and functions are `final` unless `open`; the `plugin.spring` compiler plugin opens Spring beans | [build.gradle.kts](notes/build.gradle.kts.md) |

+| Final is not immutable | `open`/`final` controls subclassing and overriding; `val`/`var` controls mutability. A final method under a Spring proxy fails silently | [build.gradle.kts](notes/build.gradle.kts.md) |
+| Platform types and `-Xjsr305=strict` | How Java nullability annotations become real `T` / `T?` types | [build.gradle.kts](notes/build.gradle.kts.md) |
+| Class with no body | `class InventoryApplication` needs no braces | [InventoryApplication.kt](notes/main/InventoryApplication.kt.md) |
+| Top-level functions | `fun main` lives outside any class; compiled into `InventoryApplicationKt` | [InventoryApplication.kt](notes/main/InventoryApplication.kt.md) |
+| Reified type parameters | `runApplication<T>()`, `withType<Test>`: the type in `<>` instead of `T::class.java` | [InventoryApplication.kt](notes/main/InventoryApplication.kt.md) |
+| Infix functions | `a version b` means `a.version(b)` | [build.gradle.kts](notes/build.gradle.kts.md) |
+| `Array<String>` | Kotlin's `String[]`: an ordinary generic class | [InventoryApplication.kt](notes/main/InventoryApplication.kt.md) |
+| Spread operator `*` | Pass an array's elements as a vararg | [InventoryApplication.kt](notes/main/InventoryApplication.kt.md) |
+| Named arguments | `proxyBeanMethods = false`, also in annotations | [TestcontainersConfiguration.kt](notes/test/support/TestcontainersConfiguration.kt.md) |
+| Expression bodies | `fun f(): T = expr` instead of `{ return expr }` | [TestcontainersConfiguration.kt](notes/test/support/TestcontainersConfiguration.kt.md) |
+| Class references `X::class` | Kotlin's version of Java's `X.class` | [InventoryApplicationTests.kt](notes/test/InventoryApplicationTests.kt.md) |
+| `internal` vs package-private | Kotlin has no package-private; `internal` = same Gradle module | [README](../../README.md#project-layout) |
+| Public by default | No modifier means `public` (Java: package-private); helpers must say `private` | [InventoryRepositoryTest.kt](notes/test/inventory/InventoryRepositoryTest.kt.md) |
+| `@Autowired constructor` | Annotating the primary constructor needs the `constructor` keyword | [InventoryRepositoryTest.kt](notes/test/inventory/InventoryRepositoryTest.kt.md) |
+| Backtick function names | `` fun `reads like a sentence`() `` for test names | [InventoryRepositoryTest.kt](notes/test/inventory/InventoryRepositoryTest.kt.md) |
+| `kotlin.test` assertions | `assertEquals`, `assertTrue`, `assertFailsWith<T> { }` | [InventoryRepositoryTest.kt](notes/test/inventory/InventoryRepositoryTest.kt.md) |
+| Extension functions | `fun MockMvc.get(...)`: a function added to a class from outside it | [InventoryControllerTest.kt](notes/test/inventory/InventoryControllerTest.kt.md) |
+| Raw strings `"""` | Multi-line strings without escaping; `trimIndent()` to strip indentation | [InventoryControllerTest.kt](notes/test/inventory/InventoryControllerTest.kt.md) |
+| Primary constructor properties | `class X(private val dep: Dep)`: declares and assigns a property in the constructor | [InventoryRepository.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryRepository.kt.md) |
+| Read-only `List` vs `MutableList` | `List` has no `add`/`remove`; callers get a snapshot | [InventoryRepository.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryRepository.kt.md) |

+| Lambdas, `_` and SAM conversion | `{ rs, _ -> ... }` stands in for Java's single-method `RowMapper`; `_` = unused parameter | [InventoryRepository.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryRepository.kt.md) |

+| A lambda's last expression is its return value | `.query { }` / `.map { }` call the lambda once per element and collect what it returns | [InventoryRepository.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryRepository.kt.md) |
+| KDoc vs `// Why:` | KDoc (`/** */`) says what, for callers, shown on hover; `// Why:` says why, for maintainers | [InventoryRepository.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryRepository.kt.md) |

+| JSpecify nullability from Java | Spring 7's `@Nullable` makes `query(Class)` yield `T?`; a row-mapper lambda keeps `T` non-null | [InventoryRepository.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryRepository.kt.md) |
+| `data class` | Generated `equals`/`hashCode`/`toString`/`copy`/`componentN` from constructor properties; Kotlin's Java `record` | [InventoryItem.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryItem.kt.md) |

+| `==` vs `===`, and `copy` | `==` calls `equals` (value equality for data classes); `===` is identity. `copy` returns a new object and leaves the original alone | [InventoryItem.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryItem.kt.md) |
+| No checked exceptions | Kotlin has no `throws` clause; unchecked `DataAccessException` travels up to a `500` | [InventoryService.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryService.kt.md) |

+| Nullable types `T?` | `InventoryItem?` = an item or `null`; the compiler makes you handle `null` before use. Kotlin's built-in `Optional` | [InventoryRepository.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryRepository.kt.md) |

+| `singleOrNull` / `single` / `firstOrNull` | Zero-or-one lookups on a list; `singleOrNull` returns `null` (no exception) for 0 *or* 2+ elements | [InventoryRepository.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryRepository.kt.md) |
+| Elvis operator `?:` | `a ?: b` = `a` unless it's `null`, then `b` | [InventoryService.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryService.kt.md) |
+| `throw` as an expression, `Nothing` | `x ?: throw E()` has the non-null type of `x`; `Nothing` fits any type | [InventoryService.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryService.kt.md) |

+| KDoc block tags (`@throws`) | Tags start their own line; `@throws` is how a signature announces an exception without checked exceptions | [InventoryService.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryService.kt.md) |
+| Extending a class | `class A(x: T) : B(...)` = `extends B` plus the `super(...)` call | [SkuNotFoundException.kt](notes/main/inventory/error/SkuNotFoundException.kt.md) |
+| Plain constructor parameters | No `val`/`var` = usable only during construction, not a property | [SkuNotFoundException.kt](notes/main/inventory/error/SkuNotFoundException.kt.md) |

+| Storage vs visibility | `val` decides whether a constructor parameter is kept; `private` decides who can read it. `private val` enforces the layers | [SkuNotFoundException.kt](notes/main/inventory/error/SkuNotFoundException.kt.md) |
+| No ternary; `if` is an expression | Java's `c ? a : b` is `if (c) a else b`; `?:` (Elvis) only tests for `null` | [InventoryService.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryService.kt.md) |
+| String templates | `"SKU not found: $skuId"`, and `${expr}` for anything longer than a name | [SkuNotFoundException.kt](notes/main/inventory/error/SkuNotFoundException.kt.md) |
+| Nullable values from Java | `Throwable.message` is `String?` because `getMessage()` may return null | [InventoryExceptionHandler.kt](notes/main/inventory/error/InventoryExceptionHandler.kt.md) |
+| Default arguments | `fun f(x: T = default)`: callers may leave the argument out; replaces Java overloads | [InventoryControllerTest.kt](notes/test/inventory/InventoryControllerTest.kt.md) |
+| Array literals in annotations | `@ValueSource(ints = [0, -5])`; Java writes `{0, -5}` | [InventoryControllerTest.kt](notes/test/inventory/InventoryControllerTest.kt.md) |

+| Generic functions and function types | `fun <T> race(action: (Int) -> T)`: a type parameter plus a parameter that holds a function | [InventoryConcurrencyTest.kt](notes/test/inventory/InventoryConcurrencyTest.kt.md) |
+| Ranges `..` and `until` | `1..n` includes `n`, `0 until n` excludes it; both work with `map`, `sum` | [InventoryConcurrencyTest.kt](notes/test/inventory/InventoryConcurrencyTest.kt.md) |
+| `runCatching` and `Result` | Runs a block and captures success or exception as a value, nothing thrown | [InventoryConcurrencyTest.kt](notes/test/inventory/InventoryConcurrencyTest.kt.md) |
+| Implicit lambda parameter `it` | A one-parameter lambda can leave the parameter out and use `it` | [InventoryConcurrencyTest.kt](notes/test/inventory/InventoryConcurrencyTest.kt.md) |
+## Spring
+| Concept | What it is | First seen |
+| `@SpringBootApplication` | `@Configuration` + `@EnableAutoConfiguration` + `@ComponentScan` from this package down | [InventoryApplication.kt](notes/main/InventoryApplication.kt.md) |
+| Starters and the Boot BOM | Starters bundle dependencies; the dependency-management plugin supplies versions | [build.gradle.kts](notes/build.gradle.kts.md) |
+| Docker Compose support | `bootRun` starts compose.yaml and wires the DataSource | [compose.yaml](notes/compose.yaml.md) |

+| Property source precedence | Command line > environment variables > application.yml > defaults; relaxed binding maps `SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL` to `spring.datasource.url` | [application.yml](notes/main/resources/application.yml.md) |
+| Connection details | Compose / Testcontainers supply the DB connection, overriding `spring.datasource.*` | [application.yml](notes/main/resources/application.yml.md) |
+| Test context caching | Identical test configurations share one context (and container) until the run ends | [TestcontainersConfiguration.kt](notes/test/support/TestcontainersConfiguration.kt.md) |
+| `@TestConfiguration` + `@Import` | Test-only beans that component scanning skips | [TestcontainersConfiguration.kt](notes/test/support/TestcontainersConfiguration.kt.md) |
+| `@ServiceConnection` | A Testcontainers container supplies DataSource connection details | [TestcontainersConfiguration.kt](notes/test/support/TestcontainersConfiguration.kt.md) |
+| `@SpringBootTest` | Starts the full application context in a test | [InventoryApplicationTests.kt](notes/test/InventoryApplicationTests.kt.md) |
+| Exception translation | SQL errors become `DataAccessException`s, e.g. `DataIntegrityViolationException` | [InventoryRepositoryTest.kt](notes/test/inventory/InventoryRepositoryTest.kt.md) |
+| `@JdbcTest` slice | JDBC-only context, no component scan, each test rolled back | [InventoryRepositoryTest.kt](notes/test/inventory/InventoryRepositoryTest.kt.md) |
+| `@AutoConfigureMockMvc` + Kotlin MockMvc DSL | In-process HTTP requests; `mockMvc.get(...).andExpect { }` | [InventoryControllerTest.kt](notes/test/inventory/InventoryControllerTest.kt.md) |
+| `JsonCompareMode.STRICT` | Exact JSON match: no extra fields, array order matters | [InventoryControllerTest.kt](notes/test/inventory/InventoryControllerTest.kt.md) |

+| Flyway migrations | `V<n>__<desc>.sql` (two underscores) in `db/migration`, run once at startup, checksummed; wrong names are skipped silently | [V1__create_inventory.sql](notes/main/resources/db/migration/V1__create_inventory.sql.md) |

+| Migrations are changes, not snapshots | A schema change is a new `V2__` with `ALTER TABLE`; the schema is the whole V1→Vn chain | [V1__create_inventory.sql](notes/main/resources/db/migration/V1__create_inventory.sql.md) |

+| Component scanning and stereotypes | `@Repository`/`@Service`/`@RestController` make scanned classes beans; `@Import` registers one by hand | [InventoryRepository.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryRepository.kt.md) |
+| Constructor injection | A single constructor is autowired without `@Autowired`; beans are created at startup | [InventoryRepository.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryRepository.kt.md) |
+| `JdbcClient` query chain | `sql(...)` prepares, `query { row mapper }` maps, `list()` runs and collects | [InventoryRepository.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryRepository.kt.md) |

+| `@RestController` vs `@Controller` | `@RestController` = `@Controller` + `@ResponseBody`: return values are written as the body, not rendered as views | [InventoryController.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryController.kt.md) |
+| `@RequestMapping` + `@GetMapping` | Class-level base path plus method-level mappings; the function name doesn't matter | [InventoryController.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryController.kt.md) |
+| Message converters (Jackson) | A `@ResponseBody` value is written as JSON; Kotlin property names become JSON keys | [InventoryController.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryController.kt.md) |
+| The service layer | Business rules and error mapping sit between HTTP (controller) and SQL (repository) | [InventoryService.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryService.kt.md) |

+| Singleton beans and threads | One bean instance, built at startup, serves every request thread at once, so beans must be stateless | [InventoryController.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryController.kt.md) |
+| Named parameters in SQL | `:skuId` + `.param("skuId", value)` binds the value separately, preventing SQL injection | [InventoryRepository.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryRepository.kt.md) |

+| `@PathVariable` and path templates | `@GetMapping("/{skuId}")` matches one path segment and binds it to the same-named parameter | [InventoryController.kt](notes/main/inventory/InventoryController.kt.md) |

+| Domain exceptions | The service throws a domain error (`SkuNotFoundException`); a handler decides the HTTP status | [SkuNotFoundException.kt](notes/main/inventory/error/SkuNotFoundException.kt.md) |

+| `@RestControllerAdvice` + `@ExceptionHandler` | One class that catches exceptions from every controller; within a class the closest exception type wins, across advice classes their `@Order` decides first | [InventoryExceptionHandler.kt](notes/main/inventory/error/InventoryExceptionHandler.kt.md) |

+| `@ParameterizedTest` + `@ValueSource` | One test method run once per supplied value, each reported separately | [InventoryControllerTest.kt](notes/test/inventory/InventoryControllerTest.kt.md) |
+| `@RepeatedTest` | Runs a test N times; used for intermittent concurrency bugs | [InventoryConcurrencyTest.kt](notes/test/inventory/InventoryConcurrencyTest.kt.md) |

+| Test transactions are per thread | A `@JdbcTest` rollback covers only the test thread; worker threads commit on their own connections | [InventoryConcurrencyTest.kt](notes/test/inventory/InventoryConcurrencyTest.kt.md) |
+| Start gate (`CountDownLatch`) | Hold N threads at one line, then release them together so they really overlap | [InventoryConcurrencyTest.kt](notes/test/inventory/InventoryConcurrencyTest.kt.md) |

+| Concept | What it is | First seen |

content.text:
Your `.param(...)` calls are right. Most of the other problems are in the SQL string, plus one missing piece at the end of the chain. Here they are in the order I'd fix them.

### 1. The string doesn't reach `sql(...)` (compile error)

Count the parentheses. `sql(` opens on line 37 and `(` opens on line 38, but the `)` on line 43 closes only the inner one. `sql(` never closes, so `.param(...)` ends up being called on the **String**.

The concatenation has a second problem: there are no spaces between the pieces. `"...quantity)" + "VALUES..."` becomes `quantity)VALUES`.

**Hint:** you've already seen the fix in the tests: a raw string, `"""..."""`. It can span lines, needs no `+` and no inner parentheses, and the line breaks become whitespace, which SQL accepts. `findBySkuId` gets away with one line; this statement is long enough to want the raw string.

### 2. `VALUES (sku_id = :skuId, :quantity)`

`VALUES` takes only the values, matched to the column list by position. `(sku_id, quantity)` already names the columns, so `VALUES` needs just the two parameters.

### 3. `ON CONFLICT (skuId)`

This is SQL, so it's the column name, not the Kotlin name. The conflict target is the primary key column.

### 4. `DO UPDATE SET quantity = :quantity` overwrites the stock

Posting 3 to a SKU with 5 would store 3, and the "adds to an existing SKU" test catches that. You need current stock plus new stock. Inside `DO UPDATE` you can refer to two rows:
- `inventory.quantity`: the row already in the table
- `EXCLUDED.quantity`: the row you tried to insert, the one that conflicted

(`:quantity` also works, since a named parameter can appear more than once. `EXCLUDED` is the usual upsert style.)

### 5. `WHERE quantity >= 0` isn't the overflow guard

- **What it checks:** the `CHECK` constraint already guarantees `>= 0`, so this line adds nothing. The guard has to answer a different question: would current plus new go past `Int.MAX_VALUE` (2147483647)?
- **Why `a + b <= MAX` won't work:** the addition itself overflows, and Postgres throws. Move the `b` to the other side of the `<=` so nothing gets added.
- **Name the table:** in this `WHERE`, a bare `quantity` is ambiguous, because both `inventory` and `EXCLUDED` have that column. Qualify every reference.
- **Optional:** bind the max as a parameter (`.param(..., Int.MAX_VALUE)`) instead of typing 2147483647. The Kotlin constant then documents itself.

### 6. No `RETURNING`

An `INSERT` returns no rows by default, so `.query { }` would have nothing to map, and Postgres errors with "No results were returned by the query". Add `RETURNING` with the two columns your row mapper reads.

### 7. Your question: how the data comes back

Walk through the three cases with `RETURNING` in place:

| Case | What Postgres does | Rows returned |
|---|---|---|
| New SKU | inserts | 1 |
| Existing SKU, guard true | updates | 1 |
| Existing SKU, guard **false** | does nothing | **0** |

So it's zero or one row, exactly like `findBySkuId`, and the same ending fits: `.list().singleOrNull()`. The empty case is how you get the `null` that means "would overflow", with no exception needed. `.single()` would be wrong here: it throws on zero rows.

### 8. Documentation

`addStock` needs KDoc: what it does, and what `null` means. It also needs a `// Why:` on the guard, because it's the kind of line a reviewer asks about in the interview.

Once it compiles, run `.\gradlew.bat test --tests "*InventoryRepositoryTest"`. The two overflow tests are the ones most likely to fail first, and their messages will point you at the guard. If you get stuck on the guard, ask for the next hint.

I am still confused by 4 and 5. How do i paramaterize what is in the database vs the quantity in the insert query so i can do math on them? Can i do math in a sql query itself?

Yes, SQL can do math. `+`, `-`, `*` and `/` work anywhere SQL expects a value: in `SELECT`, in `SET`, and in `WHERE`. Postgres works the numbers out itself, inside the statement.

The key idea is that **you only parameterize values that come from Kotlin.** The value already in the database doesn't need a parameter. You refer to it by its **column name**, and Postgres reads it from the row as it runs the statement.

| Value | Where it lives | How the SQL refers to it |
|---|---|---|
| The quantity being posted | your Kotlin `quantity` variable | a parameter: `:quantity` |
| The quantity already stored | the row in the table | the column name |

### A parallel example: a library

The table is `books(isbn, copies)`, and the library receives 3 more copies of one book. First, a plain `UPDATE`:

```sql
UPDATE books SET copies = copies + :added WHERE isbn = :isbn
```

The right side of `=` reads the row's current `copies` (say 5) and adds the parameter (3). The left side says where to store the result (8). The read and the write happen in one statement, so another request can't sneak in between them.

### Why the upsert needs two names

In `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE`, **two rows** are involved when the conflict happens:

1. the row already in the table (5 copies)
2. the row you tried to insert, which was refused because the key already exists (3 copies)

Both have a `copies` column, so a bare `copies` would be ambiguous. Postgres gives each one a name:

- `books.copies` is the existing row: **5**
- `EXCLUDED.copies` is the refused row: **3**

```sql
INSERT INTO books (isbn, copies)
VALUES (:isbn, :added)
ON CONFLICT (isbn)
DO UPDATE SET copies = books.copies + EXCLUDED.copies
RETURNING isbn, copies
```

This stores 5 + 3 = 8. The left side of `SET` stays unqualified (`copies`, not `books.copies`), because Postgres doesn't allow a table name there.

**Mapping to your code:**

| Library example | Your repository |
|---|---|
| `books` | `inventory` |
| `isbn` | `sku_id` |
| `copies` | `quantity` |
| `:isbn`, `:added` | `:skuId`, `:quantity` |

### The guard (#5): the same idea in a `WHERE`

A `WHERE` after `DO UPDATE` decides whether the update happens at all. If it's false, nothing changes and `RETURNING` gives back 0 rows, which becomes your `null`.

The rule you want is **current + new ≤ MAX**. You can't write it that way, because the `+` itself overflows. Subtract *new* from both sides instead:

**current ≤ MAX − new**

Check it with the test's numbers (MAX = 2,147,483,647):

| current | new | MAX − new | current ≤ MAX − new? | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2,147,483,646 | 1 | 2,147,483,646 | yes | update, total = MAX ✓ |
| 2,147,483,646 | 2 | 2,147,483,645 | **no** | no row → `null` ✓ |

`MAX − new` can never overflow. `new` is at least 1, so the result always stays between 0 and MAX.

**Your turn:** which of `inventory.quantity` / `EXCLUDED.quantity` is *current*, and which is *new*? And where does MAX come from: typed into the SQL, or bound with `.param` from `Int.MAX_VALUE`? Put those into `WHERE ___ <= ___ - ___`, then run the repository tests.

content.text:
Right: Postgres provides it, and you never declare it. `EXCLUDED` is a **built-in name** that exists automatically, but only inside the `ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE` part of an `INSERT`.

### A Kotlin comparison you already know

In a lambda with one parameter, you can write `it` without declaring it:

```kotlin
listOf(1, 2, 3).map { it * 2 }
```

You never wrote `val it = ...`. Kotlin supplies `it` because it knows there's exactly one value being passed in. `EXCLUDED` is the same idea in SQL. Postgres knows that during a conflict there's a "row I tried to insert", and it gives that row a ready-made name.

### What Postgres does, step by step

Take `POST /inventory/widget` with `{"quantity": 3}` when `widget` already has 5.

1. **`VALUES (:skuId, :quantity)`** builds the row you *want* to insert: `(sku_id = 'widget', quantity = 3)`.
2. Postgres tries to insert it and finds that `widget` is already in the primary key. That's a **conflict**.
3. Instead of failing, it goes to `ON CONFLICT (sku_id) DO UPDATE`. The proposed row was *excluded* (left out) from the table, hence the name, and it's now available as **`EXCLUDED`**:
   - `EXCLUDED.sku_id` = `'widget'`
   - `EXCLUDED.quantity` = `3`
4. The existing row is available under the table's name:
   - `inventory.quantity` = `5`
5. `SET quantity = inventory.quantity + EXCLUDED.quantity` computes 5 + 3 = 8 and stores it.

When there's **no** conflict (a new SKU), steps 3–5 never happen. The row is simply inserted, and `EXCLUDED` never comes up.

### The two things to remember

- **You don't set `EXCLUDED`; you fill it indirectly.** Whatever you put in `VALUES (...)` becomes `EXCLUDED`'s values. So `EXCLUDED.quantity` is the same number as your `:quantity` parameter. The two are interchangeable here, and `EXCLUDED` is just the conventional way to write an upsert.
- **It only exists inside `DO UPDATE`.** You can use it in the `SET` and in the `WHERE` that follows. Anywhere else in the statement, Postgres reports that it doesn't know the name.

Does that clear it up? If it does, you have every piece for the `SET` and the guard.

Before the `WHERE`, a few quick things in what's there now:

- **Line 38: `("` is still a regular string.** A regular `"..."` string can't span lines in Kotlin. It needs to be `"""` at the start and `"""` at the end.

(The indentation stair-step is fine; SQL doesn't care about whitespace. Lining the clauses up flush looks cleaner, but that's your call.)

The chain after the string is right now: `.param`, `.param`, `.query { }`, `.list().singleOrNull()`.

## The `WHERE` guard

### Where it goes

The `WHERE` belongs to `DO UPDATE`, so it sits **right after the `SET` line and before `RETURNING`**:

```
INSERT ...
VALUES ...
ON CONFLICT ...
DO UPDATE SET ...
WHERE ...          ← here
RETURNING ...
```

It filters only the update. For a brand-new SKU there's no conflict, so Postgres never reads this `WHERE`. That's fine, because a single `Int` can't overflow on its own.

### What it says

The rule from before is **current ≤ MAX − new**. In this statement:

| In the rule | In the SQL |
|---|---|
| current (already stored) | the existing row's quantity: `inventory.___` |
| new (being posted) | the refused row's quantity: `EXCLUDED.___` |
| MAX | see the options below |

So the shape is: `WHERE` *existing quantity* `<=` *MAX* `-` *posted quantity*.

### Where MAX comes from: two options

1. **Type it into the SQL:** `2147483647`. It works, but a reader has to recognize that number.
2. **Bind it as a parameter (my recommendation):** write `:maxQuantity` in the SQL and add a third `.param("maxQuantity", Int.MAX_VALUE)`. The Kotlin constant names itself, and if the column ever became a `BIGINT` with `Long`, there'd be one obvious place to change.

### What happens when it's false

Postgres leaves the existing row exactly as it was and **doesn't return it**. So `RETURNING` gives back 0 rows, `.list()` is empty, and `.singleOrNull()` gives `null`. The null path needs no extra code; the `WHERE` alone produces it.

Worth a `// Why:` line above the guard: the next reader will wonder why it's written as `a <= MAX - b` and not `a + b <= MAX`.

Write it, then run `.\gradlew.bat test --tests "*InventoryRepositoryTest"`. All 15 should pass. If the overflow test fails with "integer out of range", something in the guard is still adding.

```sql
WHERE inventory.quantity <= maxQuantity - EXCLUDED.quantity
```

Without the `:`, Postgres doesn't see a parameter. It reads `maxQuantity` as a **column name**, finds no such column in `inventory`, and fails with `column "maxquantity" does not exist`. - The guard is the right shape and in the right place. It's qualified `inventory.quantity` on the left and `MAX - EXCLUDED.quantity` on the right, with no addition, so it can't overflow.
- `.param("maxQuantity", Int.MAX_VALUE)` is the better of the two options.
- The mapper and `.list().singleOrNull()` are correct, and the null path works just as described.

This bug class is a good one to remember for the interview. Your concepts index has a row called "When mistakes surface": compile time for types, but **first run** for strings like SQL. I dont understand the returning. I just add the sku_id, quantity after so it returns those?

Yes. `RETURNING sku_id, quantity` is exactly it.

The easiest way to think about it: **`RETURNING` is a `SELECT` column list stuck on the end of an `INSERT` or `UPDATE`.** Compare it with `findBySkuId`:

```sql
SELECT sku_id, quantity FROM inventory WHERE ...     -- findBySkuId: reads rows
INSERT ... ON CONFLICT ... RETURNING sku_id, quantity -- addStock: writes, then hands back the row
```

Both produce a result set with the same two columns. That's why your row mapper is identical in both functions: `rs.getString("sku_id")` and `rs.getInt("quantity")` read the columns by name, so the names after `RETURNING` must match what the mapper asks for.

Three details worth knowing:

- **It returns the row *after* the change.** With 5 in stock and 3 posted, `quantity` comes back as **8**, not 3. That's the contract's "Returns the updated inventory state".
- **Without `RETURNING`, an `INSERT` returns no rows,** only a count of rows changed. To get the new total without it, you'd need a second `SELECT`, and another request could change the row between the two statements. `RETURNING` gives you the value from the same atomic statement.
- **It only returns rows that were actually written.** When the overflow guard is false, nothing is written, so `RETURNING` returns nothing: 0 rows, then `singleOrNull()`, then `null`.

Java/JDBC comparison: without `RETURNING`, you'd call `executeUpdate()` and get back just an `int` row count. With it, you call `executeQuery()` and get a `ResultSet`, like a `SELECT`. That's why this function uses `.query { }` and not `.update()`.

I have a question for the exluded value. We are subtracting it from the max quantity, but what if that value is a large positive value? What if it goes over?

Good instinct: always ask what the edge values do to arithmetic. Here the subtraction is safe, and the reason comes down to **how big `EXCLUDED.quantity` can possibly be**.

### How big can it get?

`EXCLUDED.quantity` is whatever you put in `VALUES (:skuId, :quantity)`, and `:quantity` is bound from a Kotlin `Int`. An `Int` can't hold anything above `Int.MAX_VALUE`. A request like `{"quantity": 3000000000}` never gets this far: Jackson can't fit it into an `Int` and rejects the body. One of the unreadable-body tests checks exactly that.

So the largest possible value is `MAX` itself, and the subtraction stays in range:

| `EXCLUDED.quantity` (new) | `MAX − new` | Overflow? |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2,147,483,646 | no |
| 1,000,000 | 2,147,483,647 − 1,000,000 | no |
| 2,147,483,647 (`MAX`) | **0** | no |

Subtracting a positive number from `MAX` moves *down*, toward 0. Subtraction can only overflow by going below `Int.MIN_VALUE` (about −2.1 billion). Getting there from `MAX` would take subtracting more than 4.2 billion, which no `Int` can hold.

### The biggest case works correctly too

With `new = MAX`, the guard becomes `current <= 0`:
- **The SKU is at 0:** `0 <= 0` is true, so the total becomes `MAX`. That's allowed.
- **The SKU is at anything above 0:** false, so `null` comes back. That's right, because the total would be past `MAX`.

Your repository test does exactly this: the `"full"` SKU at `MAX` plus `Int.MAX_VALUE` returns `null`.

### The real risk runs the other way: negative numbers

What *would* break the guard is a **negative** `quantity`. `MAX − (−5)` is `MAX + 5`, which overflows, and Postgres throws "integer out of range". A negative "receive" would also quietly subtract stock whenever the guard didn't trip.

So the guard is safe **only because `quantity` is always at least 1**, and the repository doesn't check that itself. It depends on the controller's validation (`@Min(1)`, still to come) to reject 0 and negatives first.

That's a precondition worth stating in the KDoc for `addStock`, for example "`quantity` must be at least 1". Then anyone calling the repository from somewhere else (a future batch import, say) knows the rule. In the interview, "what does your overflow guard assume?" is a good question to be ready for, and the answer is "that quantity is positive, which the controller enforces."

The pieces are there. Most of this is sharpening the wording, plus one comment that says something the code doesn't do.

### 1. Class KDoc (line 9) is out of date

"Reads inventory rows from Postgres": the repository **writes** now too. Easy to miss when a class grows, and `doc-reviewer` would flag it. Change "reads" to something that covers both.

### 2. `addStock` KDoc (line 37): add what a caller needs to know

What's there is accurate. A caller still needs three more things:

- **What it returns:** the row *after* the change, with the new total.
- **When it returns `null`:** the total would go past `Int.MAX_VALUE`, and nothing was changed.
- **The precondition:** `quantity` must be at least 1 (from your question just now).

"Atomic" or "in one statement" is also worth a word, since that's the concurrency guarantee. The `null` case matters most: right now, a reader of the signature `InventoryItem?` has to read the SQL to find out what `null` means. Compare it with `findBySkuId`'s KDoc, which does say when it returns `null`.

### 3. The `// Why:` on line 39 describes *what*, and it says one misleading thing

- **"Below we have the sql…"** is narration. The reader can see the SQL; the standard says `// Why:` is for decisions.
- **"Quantity must be at least 1…"** reads as if the guard enforces it. It doesn't: the guard only checks the upper limit, and the controller enforces the minimum. Move that sentence to the KDoc as the precondition (point 2).
- **The actual decision is missing:** why the guard is written as `quantity <= max - new` and not `quantity + new <= max`. That's the line a reviewer will stop on.

Aim for one or two short lines. Roughly: "guard written as current ≤ max − new because current + new would itself overflow in Postgres."

Optional second `// Why:`: one upsert instead of find-then-insert-or-update, so concurrent requests can't race.

### 4. Lines 49 and 56 are copies of `findBySkuId`'s comments

- **Line 49 (SQL injection):** the decision is the same one already explained on line 28. Repeating a `// Why:` for each function adds noise. You can delete it.
- **Line 56:** the copied reason doesn't fit here. `addStock` returns at most one row because it writes one row, not because of the primary key lookup. The `singleOrNull` here also has a *new* job: an empty list means the guard refused the update, and that's what becomes `null`. If you keep a comment on this line, that's the decision worth recording.

### What's good

- The `// Study notes:` header is in place.
- `.param("maxQuantity", Int.MAX_VALUE)` documents itself, so it needs no comment.
- KDoc sits directly above `fun`, with no comment between them. That was the session-5 slip, and it's fixed here.

When you've updated it, I'll look once more, and then it's ready to commit.
